Before Trading Point, Constantinos Cleanthous studied business mathematics and statistics, followed by a master's degree in shipping, trade and finance. That quantitative and commercial training became the foundation for his move into online financial services.

He helped establish Trading Point in 2009 as a brokerage group designed to give retail clients access to international markets. Its regulated entities developed online foreign-exchange and investment products under several brands. Cleanthous combined the durable founder role with executive responsibility as group chief executive and an indirect ownership interest documented through the US business. Those records distinguish his stake in the brokerage platform from the client funds, trading instruments and corporate assets administered by its operating companies.

uncertainties.detail: A Cypriot anaesthesiologist and other professionals share the name Constantinos Cleanthous. The target is distinguished by the exact Trading Point and XM company links, the August 1974 birth month and year, the Cypriot nationality and the Trading.com Markets UK appointment. Medical-profile sources were excluded.

The April 2025 disclosure identifies Cleanthous as an indirect owner and Trading Point Group chief executive while saying he has no day-to-day role in the separate U.S. affiliate. The dossier preserves that distinction and does not transfer a U.S. operating role to him.

The source owner record lists the United Kingdom as his main residence, while a current Companies House appointment lists Greece. Because corporate-filed country of residence does not by itself establish his principal personal residence and the value may change, no correction is proposed.
Companies House corroborates the existing August 1974 birth month and year. No sufficiently reliable source reviewed supplied a birth day or specific birthplace, so neither missing field is proposed.

Client deposits, funds, traded instruments, brokerage volumes, operating-company assets and any property held by separate companies are not treated as Cleanthous's personal property. His wealth classification follows the documented founder and indirect-owner interest, not the gross scale of assets handled by the group.

The existing LinkedIn URL matches the exact name and lists XM experience, but the public profile is sparse and was not needed as evidence. No identity-secure personal Instagram or personal website was found; the official leadership page is proposed only as a Company Website.

Politics, controversies, allegations, legal matters, sanctions, irrelevant private-family detail and all private-vessel research were excluded. None contributes to the identity, classification or biography claims.
